promptState.text:
subject_definitions:
<Picture 1> is the first frame and composition anchor for [Shot 1], defining the complete visible image exactly as supplied, including the framing, camera viewpoint, subject placement, subject scale, crop, foreground-to-background relationship, whatever forms the area behind and around the subject, lighting, shadows, colors, gradients, depth cues, and overall scene composition. Its rendering style, whether photographic, illustrated, stylised, or three-dimensional, is part of what is preserved.
<Subject 1> is the woman defined by <Picture 1>. Her face, facial structure, hair, skin tone, body shape and proportions stay exactly the same in every frame; only her clothes change, as described below.
<Subject 2> is the complete visible area behind, beneath, beside, and around <Subject 1> as defined by <Picture 1>, preserving its exact colors, surfaces, objects if any are present, spatial layout, lighting, shadows, gradients, and depth. Whatever that area looks like in <Picture 1> is exactly what it looks like in the target video, including its overall tone and brightness, and it is never exchanged for a different kind of surrounding. If objects are present, exactly those objects remain, and no further ones appear.

summary:
[keyframe completion] The target video begins from <Picture 1> and animates <Subject 1> spinning around once on the spot in one continuous fixed-camera shot; during the spin her clothes change into the new outfit shown at the end of the clip, while <Subject 1> and the complete visible area represented by <Subject 2> stay the same.

retention_analysis:
<Picture 1> ([Shot 1] first frame): fully_preserved - the supplied image is the starting frame, retaining its viewpoint, framing, subject placement, surroundings, lighting, and rendering style.
<Subject 1> (appears in [Shot 1]): partially_preserved - her face, hair, skin tone and body stay the same; her clothes change into the new outfit during the spin.
<Subject 2> (appears in [Shot 1]): fully_preserved - the referenced surroundings remain visually identical, with nothing substituted, added, or removed.

detailed_description:
The target video develops directly from the complete supplied image in <Picture 1>, preserving its rendering style, color treatment, lighting, composition, and full visible scene. <Picture 1> is the actual starting frame.
[Shot 1] The shot begins from <Picture 1>, with <Subject 1> in the clothes shown there. The camera stays still at the same height for the whole clip, with no zoom and no pan. <Subject 1> smiles, lifts her arms a little and spins around once on the spot in a quick, smooth full turn. While her back is turned to the camera her clothes change, and when she faces the camera again she is wearing the new outfit she wears at the end of the clip. She finishes the turn facing the camera, puts one hand on her hip and smiles. Her face, hair, skin tone and body shape stay exactly the same in every frame, and her hair swings naturally with the turn. <Subject 2> remains stable throughout, with no transformation, replacement, recoloring, or change of location.

overall_soundscape:
A soft whoosh of air as she spins, then quiet room tone. No speech, no voice.

non_diegetic_music:
[MUSIC]

Flux 2 Klein 9B model card

 Load Diffusion Model

Download minimax_h3_audio_vae_fp32.safetensors577 MB

{"version":1,"content":"

HOW TO USE

One Run, two models: Flux Klein dresses the person from your picture in a new outfit, then MiniMax H3 makes a video where she turns around once and ends in that outfit. Your picture is the first frame, Klein's picture the last.

 Steps

  1. 1. Load your picture: a person standing, facing the camera, from the knees up or the whole body.
  2. 2. In Find and Replace, describe the new outfit and who is in the picture.
  3. 3. Seed: F (fixed) or R (random). One seed drives both the picture and the video.
  4. 4. Pick how many seconds.
  5. 5. Leave the video size at 864 to start.
  6. 6. Describe the music, or write N/A for none.
  7. Press Run.

 The new outfit

  • Name every piece with its colour and material, like the demo: a fitted pink cotton t-shirt with the word "PIXA" ..., tucked into a white pleated midi skirt.
  • Words on clothes: put them in quotes and say the letters' size, colour and placement. Klein spelled PIXA right on 4 of 4 seeds, and it stayed readable at the end of every test video.
  • Klein keeps the face, the pose, the place and the light: only the clothes change. Its picture is saved too, so you can check it.

 Good to know

  • In the tests (4 seeds) she turned around once and ended in the new outfit on all 4; the clothes change while her back is turned.
  • H3 makes the music from the sentence in step 6.
  • The person must be easy to see whole: a person far away or cut off at the waist gives the spin less to work with.
  • Another seed gives another picture AND another spin.

 Something not working?

Each button opens the answer on the Pixaroma help page.

Save to your own folder Nodes look different from the video

{"version":1,"content":"

WHAT EACH NODE DOES

The colour of a node tells you what kind of node it is. Nothing here needs changing except the blue ones.

 Models to download

Orange. Each one needs a file from the Download Models note.

  • Load Diffusion Model (Flux 2 Klein 9B, the picture) - The image model, Flux 2 Klein 9B from Black Forest Labs (the same file as workflow 01). It makes the picture of the new outfit, the LAST frame of the video.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen 3 8B, reads the picture prompt) - Reads your prompt and turns the words into something the image model understands.
  • Load VAE (Flux 2) - Turns the finished render into a picture you can see, and a picture into the model's own format.
  • Load Diffusion Model (MiniMax H3 ref2va) - MiniMax H3, the video model. This is its Reference to Video version: besides your prompt it can look at pictures and at a video you give it.
  • Load CLIP (Qwen3-VL, reads prompt and pictures) - Qwen3-VL 32B: reads your prompt and looks at your picture.
  • Load VAE (video) - Turns the finished render into video frames, and your video into the model's own format.
  • Load VAE (sound) - Turns sound into the model's format and back.
  • LoRA Loader Pixaroma (speed) - Holds the DMAD 4-step speed LoRA: 4 steps instead of 20, same look.

 The steps you set

Blue, and numbered. These are the only nodes you need to touch.

  • Load Image Pixaroma (1. your picture, the first frame) - Your picture: a person standing, facing the camera, from the knees up or the whole body. It is the FIRST frame of the video, and Klein dresses this same picture in the new outfit for the LAST frame.
  • Find and Replace Pixaroma (2. the new outfit) - Two short boxes: the new outfit, every piece with its colour, and who is in the picture (woman, man, girl...). They fill the picture prompt below.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (the picture prompt, leave it) - The picture prompt for Klein: change only the clothes, keep the face, the pose, the place and the light. Leave it as it is.
  • Seed Pixaroma (3. random or fixed, picture and video) - The seed. F (fixed) gives the same result every Run, R (random) a new one each Run.
  • Duration Pixaroma (4. how many seconds) - How many seconds the video lasts, turned into the frame count H3 accepts.
  • Longest Side Pixaroma (5. video size) - The size of the video by its longest side; your picture keeps its shape. 864 is the default and fast; 1024 and 1280 are sharper but slower. The step is 32 because H3 needs sizes that are multiples of 32.
  • Find and Replace Pixaroma (6. the music) - One box: the music H3 makes for the video (the instruments, the mood, the tempo). Write N/A for no music.
  • Prompt Pixaroma (the video prompt, leave it) - The trained video prompt: your picture is the first frame, she turns around once, and her clothes change into the outfit of the last frame while her back is turned. Leave it as it is.

 Working in the background

Teal. They run by themselves: they make the steps faster, hand memory back, lock the real sound into the render or guide the moves. The line next to each one says if there is anything worth changing.

  • Free VRAM Pixaroma (Klein out, before H3) - Hands the graphics card memory back after Klein, so H3 has the room it needs.
  • MiniMaxH3SigmaShift (12 / 3 for the speed LoRA) - The noise schedule for the speed LoRA: 12 for the picture, 3 for the sound. Leave it as it is.
  • Model Attention Backend (faster steps) - Picks the attention maths. comfy kitchen attention makes each step about 1.7 times faster on NVIDIA and AMD cards with the same look (measured). If you get an error with it, pick pytorch attention.
  • Free VRAM Pixaroma (before the decode) - Hands the graphics card's memory back between the render and the video decode, so the decode fits on smaller cards.

 The work

Green. They run by themselves.

  • CLIP Text Encode (reads the edit prompt) - Reads the prompt through the text encoder.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. Klein runs at CFG 1, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • VAE Encode (picture to latent) - Turns your picture into the model's format so Klein can look at it.
  • ReferenceLatent (your picture, positive) - Hands your picture to Klein as the picture to edit. There are two, one for the prompt and one for the empty negative, and both get the same picture.
  • ReferenceLatent (your picture, negative) - Hands your picture to Klein as the picture to edit. There are two, one for the prompt and one for the empty negative, and both get the same picture.
  • Empty Flux 2 Latent (blank canvas) - The blank canvas the picture is painted on, at the size it receives.
  • KSampler (4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings Klein is made for.
  • VAE Decode (latent to picture) - Turns the finished render into a picture.
  • Upscale Image (the outfit picture at the video size) - Brings Klein's picture to the exact video size, so it can be the last frame.
  • Get Image Size (the video size, after Klein) - Hands the video size to H3 from Klein's picture, so the video starts only after the picture is ready.
  • MiniMaxH3ReferenceToVideo (prompt + your picture) - Builds the empty video at your size and length and reads the prompt together with your picture (<Picture 1>).
  • MiniMaxH3AddGuide (the outfit picture, last frame) - Puts Klein's picture at the LAST frame (frame_idx -1), so the video ends exactly on the new outfit.
  • ConditioningZeroOut (empty negative) - An empty negative prompt. H3 runs at CFG 1 here, where the negative does nothing, but the KSampler still needs one plugged in.
  • KSampler (video, 4 steps) - The render: 4 steps, CFG 1, euler, simple, the settings the speed LoRA is made for.
  • VAE Decode (render to video frames) - Turns the finished render into video frames.
  • VAE Decode Audio (the music) - Turns the sound H3 made, the music, into audio for the saved video.

 The result

Dark red, at the end.

  • Save Image Pixaroma (the new outfit, the last frame) - Saves Klein's picture of the new outfit into ComfyUI/output/Outfit Spin, so you can see the last frame before the video is done.
  • Save Video Pixaroma (the spin) - Saves the video as MP4 into ComfyUI/output/Outfit Spin with the music, and plays it on the node.

 Readouts

Dark. Nothing to set: they show you what happened.

  • Run Timer - The dark clock above the result shows how long the last Run took.

{"version":1,"content":"

RUN TIMES

Measured on a 24 GB RTX 4090 with this workflow, with the models already loaded. A different card gives different numbers, but the shape holds: the time grows with the size and with the seconds.

Video size5 seconds
864 (480 x 864), the defaultabout 30 s (Klein and H3 together)

Times are with comfy kitchen attention (the default here). With pytorch attention the render part takes about 1.7 times as long.

Klein and H3 take turns on the graphics card here, so every Run moves both of them in and out. The time above includes that.

 The first Run of the session

The first Run after starting ComfyUI also has to load the models (about 20 GB for H3 and 15 GB for its text encoder), so it takes longer. After that they stay loaded.
